theme: A Level Religious Studies - festivals in islam
enonce_markdown: Eid al-Fitr is celebrated by Muslims to mark:

choix.texte: the end of the Hajj pilgrimage.
the beginning of the Islamic New Year.
the end of the month of fasting, Ramadan.
the birth of the Prophet Muhammad.

corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Link each major Islamic festival with the event it marks.

### Solution

Eid al-Fitr, the festival of breaking the fast, begins on the first day of Shawwal and marks the end of Ramadan. The Hajj ends around Eid al-Adha, the New Year is the first of Muharram, and the Prophet's birthday is remembered at the Mawlid.

theme: A Level Religious Studies - festivals in islam
enonce_markdown: State **two** ways in which Muslims celebrate Eid al-Fitr.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Recall the religious and social practices of the day.

### Solution

Any two of:

- Taking a bath, wearing new or best clothes and eating a little before going out.
- Attending the special Eid prayer, usually with a sermon, in the mosque or in an open space.
- Giving zakat al-fitr to the poor before the Eid prayer.
- Visiting relatives, sharing meals and exchanging gifts and greetings.

theme: A Level Religious Studies - festivals in islam

choix.texte: A charitable gift given before the Eid al-Fitr prayer so that the poor can also celebrate.
A tax on yearly savings paid only by pilgrims at Makkah.
The sacrifice of an animal on the tenth day of Dhul-Hijjah.
A payment made to make up for missed daily prayers.

corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Identify the purpose and the timing of the obligation, then match them to the festival.

### Solution

Zakat al-fitr is a small charity given on behalf of each member of a household, normally before the Eid prayer, so that the needy can share in the festival. The animal sacrifice belongs to Eid al-Adha and is different from this charity.

theme: A Level Religious Studies - festivals in islam
enonce_markdown: A family in Garoua offers a sheep as qurbani at Eid al-Adha. According to the commonly taught practice, how is the meat usually shared?

choix.texte: All of it is given to the mosque committee for sale.
All of it is kept by the family for the festival meals.
It is divided only among the male relatives of the household.
One part for the family, one part for relatives and friends, and one part for the poor.

corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Qurbani combines worship with charity, so its meat is shared outside the household.

### Solution

The commonly taught practice divides the meat into three parts: family, relatives and friends, and the poor. This turns the festival into an act of sharing. The other options remove either the charity or the sharing with others.

theme: A Level Religious Studies - festivals in islam
enonce_markdown: Explain **two** reasons why Eid al-Adha is linked with the Hajj.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Connect the date and the rites of the festival with the pilgrimage and with the story of Ibrahim.

### Solution

- **Same time.** Eid al-Adha falls on the tenth day of Dhul-Hijjah, the month of the Hajj. It follows the day of Arafat, and pilgrims offer their sacrifices at the time when Muslims elsewhere celebrate the festival.
- **Same story.** The sacrifice recalls Ibrahim's readiness to obey God by offering his son, who was ransomed with a ram. The rites of the Hajj also recall Ibrahim, Hajar and Ismail.

Other valid points: Muslims who are not on pilgrimage join the pilgrims in spirit by praying and sacrificing, so that the whole ummah shares the occasion.

theme: A Level Religious Studies - festivals in islam
enonce_markdown: Which comparison of Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha is accurate?

choix.texte: The first falls on the tenth of Dhul-Hijjah and the second at the end of Ramadan.
Both include a special congregational prayer; the first follows the fast of Ramadan, while the second recalls Ibrahim's obedience and falls in Dhul-Hijjah.
Both festivals commemorate Ibrahim's sacrifice and differ only in the animal offered.
Only the first has a special prayer, while the second is observed with the sacrifice alone.

corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Compare festivals on four points: date, event commemorated, main rites and shared features.

### Solution

Both festivals begin with a special prayer. Eid al-Fitr, on the first of Shawwal, ends the fast of Ramadan. Eid al-Adha, on the tenth of Dhul-Hijjah, recalls Ibrahim's obedience and includes the sacrifice. The first distractor swaps the dates; the others wrongly merge the meanings or deny the prayer.
